rows.description: A child squirms and grabs while waiting for a swing or a sweet. Patience at this age is a muscle just starting, helped by counting, songs and short waits.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A child chooses to save pocket money for a bigger toy instead of spending it. Choosing later over now grows with practice and with trust that promised rewards actually arrive.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A quick child sighs at a slower classmate's struggle. Patience with others needs seeing that pace differs, and it is learned mostly by watching adults deal with slowness kindly.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 13–17, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager wants independence, results and adult status immediately and resents waiting. Long timelines feel unbearable at this age, and small milestones make them tolerable.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 23–26

rows.description: A young adult explaining a phone app to a parent for the third time keeps a steady tone. Patience is a form of respect returning what was once received in childhood.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17

rows.description: A person waits and waits for a promotion or apology, calling it patience while avoiding a needed conversation. Real patience is active and has a limit.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 13–17

rows.description: A child loses a game, feels the sting, but shakes hands or asks for a rematch. Humility begins as tolerating defeat without collapsing or blaming.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 7–12, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A child admits an error to a friend and finds the friendship survives. Discovering that being wrong is survivable is what makes humility possible.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 13–17, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A teenager confuses humility with hiding achievements and denying talent. True humility sees strengths and limits accurately, without inflating or shrinking.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26

rows.description: A peer who boasts loudly and never concedes may be guarding a fragile sense of worth. Confident people can afford to say they do not know.
graph_context: this subtopic also appears at ages: 4–6, 7–12, 18–22, 23–26
